name: DIY Cultured Buttermilk

cookwares.name: mason jar or other glass container

instructions.primary_message: In a mason jar or other glass container, thoroughly mix the starter and milk. Cover with a coffee filter or piece of cheese cloth (do not seal tightly with a lid) and leave to culture out of drafts at a warm room temperature (between 70-26°C or 21-26°C is recommended) until milk has clabbered (10-24 hours).

To test if the milk has thickened, tip the jar slightly. It should move away from the wall of the jar as a single mass. Just as with yogurt making, once the milk sets, it will get more tart the longer you allow the culturing to continue.
Refrigerate to halt culturing for at least 6 hours. Stir before using.

schema_metadata.keywords: buttermilk, diy, DIY vs Buy, milk

description: Talk about set it and forget it: The only skill culturing your own buttermilk requires is patience.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 day 6 hr 5 min.

Notes: You can make larger (or smaller) volumes as needed. I use a ratio of one tablespoon starter for every cup milk with reliable results. Unless your culture was not designed to be perpetuated (some freeze-dried options fall into this category), you can reserve a bit of each batch to culture the next.
Some recipes indicate that you should pasteurize your milk (at 82°C) before culturing or at least warm it to 24°C. This step is entirely unnecessary, as store-bought milk is all pasteurized before it hits the shelves.
author: Molly Sheridan
